To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
emergence and robustness are two important concepts that can be applied to conservation.

the conditions that enable emergence and robustness of conservation actions are 1) a balance between external guidance and enabling local actors, 2) recognition that change is needed, 3) expectation that positive outcomes will occur and 4) the ability to experiment to achieve a collective understanding of the problem and its solutions.
emergence and robustness provide a useful framework for understanding how to enable local actors to develop solutions to address threats to conservation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conditions for emergence of conservation actions at the local level and how these can be supported.
the question of how conservation can emerge from within the local community.
how to enable the emergence of robust actions for conservation in the face of limited resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conditions of emergence and robustness are important in conservation and that the CAMPFIRE programme is a good example of this.
the emergence of robust actions is a complex, dynamic, and context-dependent process.
the conditions for emergence and robustness of conservation action are complex, and need to be considered in the context of the particular social-ecological system in question.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CAMPFIRE model is a good example of how a conservation program can support local people to self-organize and take ownership of their own conservation initiatives, but that the balance between external guidance and local autonomy is difficult to manage, and needs to be adapted over time.

the emergence of conservation actions is a process that is enabled by the presence of certain conditions and that the process itself can be supported and facilitated by the provision of appropriate external guidance.

we are not suggesting that the CAMPFIRE programme has failed, but rather that we need to learn from the programme's successes and failures to better understand the factors that influence the emergence of robust actions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
conservationists need to be aware of the conditions for the emergence of robust actions, and that the balance of these conditions needs to be managed carefully over time.

conservation practitioners should focus their efforts on creating enabling conditions for emergence and robustness, and not necessarily on the design of the specific activities and initiatives that will be implemented.
the conditions for emergence can be supported by providing external guidance and enabling local actors.
